title: Laredo's $2.6 Billion Building Boom: 162 Projects Registered in a Year
excerpt: Laredo has 162 construction projects registered over the past year, worth an estimated $2.6 billion combined, with more than 24 openings expected in the next 120 days.
content:
Laredo is in the middle of a building boom. New state records show 162 construction projects registered in the city over the past 12 months, with a combined estimated value of $2.6 billion — and more than 24 of them are expected to open in the next 120 days.

The figures come from Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation (TDLR) project records, aggregated by the construction tracker Zabalist in its November 2026 report for Laredo. The report was updated November 15.

What the numbers show

New construction dominates the activity. Of the 162 registered projects, 78 — just over 48 percent — are new construction. The rest are renovations, alterations and other registered work.

At least 24 projects passed their TDLR accessibility inspection or closed out their filings in the past 90 days, a strong signal that construction has finished. And at least 24 more are tracked with completion estimated in the next 120 days, including LITOS TI, EVOLVE FITNESS CLUB and Daneze, LLC. Estimated completion dates come from TDLR filings and change as construction progresses.

The design firms and developers with the most registered projects in Laredo over the past year include GMA Architects, Redline Architecture and Align Design Associates, according to the report.

What it means — and what it doesn't

A filing with the state is a milestone, not a guarantee. Zabalist notes that a passed inspection or a closed filing does not independently confirm that a business is open, and completion estimates are based on filings, not on-site checks.

Still, the scale is the story: $2.6 billion of registered work in a single year in a city of Laredo's size is a major bet on growth — on trade, on housing, on retail and services. The open questions now are the ones that matter to residents: how many of these projects bring lasting local jobs, how the growth lands on roads and neighborhoods, and how many of the "opening soon" projects actually open on time.

Webb Watch 956 will keep tracking the openings as they happen — and checking which ones deliver what was promised.

Sources:

  • Zabalist — Laredo Construction & New Openings Report, November 2026
  • Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation (TDLR) project records
